intentions: Define customer and order data models with attributes such as name, email, order ID, items, and status.
Separate data access logic into repositories for customer and order persistence using a database or file-based storage.
Implement business rules in the service layer, such as order validation, customer existence checks, and order status transitions.
Create a command-line interface (CLI) to allow users to add, view, update, and delete customers and orders.
Ensure modularity by organizing code into distinct modules: models, repositories, services, and CLI.
Enforce separation of concerns: models define data structure, repositories handle data access, services manage business logic, and CLI provides user interaction.
Allow for future extension by enabling integration with different databases or APIs through abstraction in repositories and services.
